newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma urges government to pay off wages.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma urges government to pay off wages.

text.p: The State Duma lower house of parliament called on the government on Friday to draw up plans within weeks to pay 9.3 trillion roubles owed in pensions and back wages to public-sector employees.

The Duma passed a resolution unanimously demanding that the government present plans to the Duma by March for paying off the massive arrears in wages and pensions, the official Itar-Tass news agency said.
The resolution is not binding but is an expression of widespread outrage at the failure of the government and companies to pay wages and pensions on time.
The public-sector arrears affect not only pensioners but also teachers, doctors, students, miners and the military, who receive their salaries from the federal government.

President Boris Yeltsin said on Friday that pensions would be paid on time from now on and all arrears would be cleared, and Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said the government planned to settle its debts to pensioners by July 1 this year.
"We have two goals: from February 1 we have to stop the debt from growing, but most important is to repay the main body of debt which will be done by July 1," Livshits told reporters.
Deputy Finance Minister Izosim Molchanov told the Duma the government would pay a total of 15.3 trillion roubles to pay off its all its debts by July 1 this year, Itar-Tass said.
Molchanov said wage arrears were one of the most severe social problems facing Russia, but January tax receipts were enough to cover only the salaries of employees of the central ministries.
Tax collection is a severe problem for the government, which at the end of last year set up an emergency committee to enforce compliance from Russian companies in arrears.
